title: Bahia Palace
content:
# Bahia Palace

## Overview

Bahia Palace is one of Morocco's finest examples of traditional Moroccan architecture. Built during the late nineteenth century, it features beautiful courtyards, intricate tilework, carved cedar ceilings, and peaceful gardens.

## Location

City: Marrakech

## Highlights

- Traditional Moroccan architecture
- Decorative mosaics
- Interior courtyards
- Orange tree gardens
- Historic royal residence

## Visiting Information

The palace can be explored independently or with a local guide.

## Estimated Visit Duration

1–2 hours

## Photography

Photography is permitted in most public areas.

## Nearby Attractions

- Jemaa el-Fnaa
- El Badi Palace
- Saadian Tombs

## Travel Tips

- Visit early to enjoy quieter surroundings.
- Read the historical displays for additional context.
- Combine your visit with nearby attractions.

title: Hassan II Mosque
content:
# Hassan II Mosque

## Overview

The Hassan II Mosque is one of Morocco's most iconic landmarks and one of the largest mosques in the world. Located on the Atlantic coast in Casablanca, part of the mosque is built over the ocean, making it a unique architectural masterpiece.

## Location

City: Casablanca

## Highlights

- World's tallest minaret (approximately 210 metres)
- Capacity for over 100,000 worshippers
- Traditional Moroccan craftsmanship
- Oceanfront location
- Large prayer hall
- Beautiful marble floors and cedar wood ceilings

## Visiting Information

Non-Muslim visitors may enter only through guided tours outside prayer times.

It is recommended to book guided tours in advance during peak tourist seasons.

## Opening Hours

Opening hours vary depending on the season and religious events.

Visitors should verify schedules before arriving.

## Dress Code

Visitors should wear modest clothing.

Shoes must be removed before entering designated areas.

## Photography

Photography is generally permitted in visitor areas.

Flash photography may be restricted during guided tours.

## Accessibility

The mosque is accessible to visitors with reduced mobility.

## Nearby Attractions

- La Corniche
- Morocco Mall
- Habous Quarter
- Arab League Park

## Travel Tips

- Visit in the morning for fewer crowds.
- Arrive at least 30 minutes before the guided tour.
- Bring a light jacket during windy weather.

title: Jardin Majorelle
content:
# Jardin Majorelle

## Overview

Jardin Majorelle is a botanical garden in Marrakech famous for its vibrant blue buildings, exotic plants, and peaceful atmosphere. It was designed by French artist Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent and Pierre Bergé.

## Location

City: Marrakech

## Highlights

- Exotic plants from five continents
- Famous Majorelle Blue architecture
- Bamboo gardens
- Cactus collection
- Water features
- Islamic Art Museum

## Visiting Information

The garden is one of Marrakech's most visited attractions.

Online ticket reservations are recommended.

## Opening Hours

Open daily.

Opening hours may vary depending on the season.

## Estimated Visit Duration

1–2 hours

## Photography

Photography is allowed throughout most areas.

## Nearby Attractions

- Yves Saint Laurent Museum
- Gueliz District
- Koutoubia Mosque
- Jemaa el-Fnaa

## Travel Tips

- Visit early in the morning to avoid crowds.
- Bring water during summer.
- Wear comfortable walking shoes.

title: Jemaa el-Fnaa
content:
# Jemaa el-Fnaa

## Overview

Jemaa el-Fnaa is the central square of Marrakech and one of Morocco's most vibrant cultural spaces. It transforms throughout the day, offering markets, food stalls, musicians, storytellers, and street performances.

## Location

City: Marrakech

## Highlights

- Traditional food stalls
- Fresh fruit juice vendors
- Snake charmers
- Henna artists
- Street musicians
- Local crafts

## Best Time to Visit

Late afternoon and evening when the square becomes most active.

## Food

Visitors can enjoy:

- Tagine
- Grilled meats
- Harira
- Moroccan pastries
- Fresh orange juice

## Safety

The square is generally safe but crowded.

Visitors should watch personal belongings and agree on prices before purchasing services.

## Nearby Attractions

- Koutoubia Mosque
- Bahia Palace
- El Badi Palace
- Marrakech Souks

## Estimated Visit Duration

2–4 hours

## Travel Tips

- Carry cash.
- Negotiate prices politely.
- Ask permission before photographing performers.

title: Volubilis
content:
# Volubilis

## Overview

Volubilis is Morocco's best-preserved Roman archaeological site and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It contains impressive ruins including temples, basilicas, triumphal arches, and beautifully preserved mosaics.

## Location

Near Meknes

## Highlights

- Roman mosaics
- Triumphal Arch
- Basilica
- Capitol Temple
- Ancient olive presses

## Historical Importance

Volubilis was an important Roman city from the first century AD and remains one of North Africa's most significant archaeological sites.

## Visiting Information

Visitors can explore independently or hire local certified guides.

## Estimated Visit Duration

2–3 hours

## Photography

Photography is permitted throughout the archaeological site.

## Nearby Attractions

- Meknes
- Moulay Idriss Zerhoun

## Travel Tips

- Wear comfortable walking shoes.
- Bring water during warmer months.
- Morning visits are recommended to avoid high temperatures.

title: Casablanca
content:
# Casablanca

## Overview

Casablanca is Morocco's largest city and its economic capital. Located on the Atlantic coast, it is a modern metropolis combining business districts, historical neighborhoods, and cultural landmarks.

## Why Visit

- Largest city in Morocco
- Home to the Hassan II Mosque
- Modern shopping centers
- Corniche beachfront
- Vibrant nightlife
- Business and financial hub

## Main Attractions

- Hassan II Mosque
- Morocco Mall
- The Corniche
- Habous Quarter
- Arab League Park
- Old Medina

## Transportation

Casablanca has one of Morocco's best public transport systems.

Available transport:
- Casa Tramway
- Taxis
- ONCF trains
- Buses
- Ride-hailing services

## Best Time to Visit

March–May and September–November offer pleasant temperatures.

## Local Cuisine

- Seafood
- Couscous
- Tagine
- Pastilla

## Safety

Casablanca is generally safe. Visitors should remain aware of pickpockets in crowded markets and tourist areas.

## Recommended Stay

2–3 days

title: Fes
content:

title: Emergency Numbers in Morocco
content:
# Emergency Numbers in Morocco

## Overview

Morocco has several national emergency numbers that visitors can use to contact police, medical services, and fire departments. If possible, explain your location clearly and provide nearby landmarks.

## National Emergency Numbers

### General Emergency

112

Available for emergency assistance and can be used from most mobile phones.

### Police

19 (Urban Areas)

177 (From Mobile Phones)

Contact the police for crimes, theft, suspicious activity, or immediate public safety concerns.

### Royal Gendarmerie

177

Responsible for law enforcement in rural areas and on many highways.

### Ambulance and Medical Emergencies

15

Call for urgent medical assistance.

### Fire Brigade

15

Contact the fire service for fires, rescue operations, or hazardous situations.

## Tourist Police

Tourist police operate in many major tourist destinations, including:

- Marrakech
- Casablanca
- Rabat
- Fes
- Tangier
- Agadir

They assist international visitors with safety concerns, lost property, and tourist-related incidents.

## If You Lose Your Passport

If your passport is lost or stolen:

1. Report the incident to the nearest police station.
2. Obtain a police report.
3. Contact your country's embassy or consulate.
4. Follow the embassy's instructions to obtain emergency travel documents.

## Useful Advice

- Save emergency numbers before travelling.
- Keep copies of your passport and travel insurance.
- Share your itinerary with family or friends.
- Learn the address of your accommodation.
- In an emergency, remain calm and provide clear information about your location.

## Languages

Emergency operators may speak Arabic and French. English may be available in major cities but is not guaranteed.

title: Medical Services and Hospitals in Morocco
content:
# Medical Services and Hospitals in Morocco

## Overview

Major Moroccan cities have public and private hospitals, clinics, pharmacies, and emergency medical services. Private hospitals generally offer shorter waiting times and are commonly used by international visitors.

## Public Hospitals

Public hospitals are available throughout Morocco and provide emergency care.

Services include:

- Emergency treatment
- General medicine
- Surgery
- Maternity care
- Specialist consultations

Waiting times may be longer during busy periods.

## Private Clinics

Private clinics are common in major cities and usually provide:

- Emergency consultations
- Medical imaging
- Laboratory testing
- Specialist appointments
- Surgical procedures

Travel insurance may cover treatment at private facilities depending on the policy.

## Pharmacies

Pharmacies are widely available in Moroccan cities and towns.

Many pharmacists can provide advice for minor illnesses and over-the-counter medication.

Some medications require a prescription.

## Medical Advice for Travellers

Seek medical attention immediately if you experience:

- Chest pain
- Difficulty breathing
- Severe allergic reactions
- Serious injuries
- High fever lasting several days
- Signs of dehydration

## Travel Insurance

Visitors are strongly encouraged to obtain travel insurance that includes:

- Emergency medical treatment
- Hospitalisation
- Medical evacuation
- Repatriation
- Trip interruption

## Useful Information

Carry the following information during your trip:

- Passport
- Travel insurance details
- Emergency contact information
- List of allergies
- Current medications
- Blood type (if known)

## Health Tips

- Drink bottled or safe drinking water if unsure about water quality.
- Use sunscreen during summer months.
- Stay hydrated, especially in hot regions.
- Carry essential medications in their original packaging.
- Seek medical advice before travelling if you have chronic health conditions.

title: FAQ: Airports in Morocco
content:
# FAQ: Airports in Morocco

## What are Morocco's main international airports?

Major international airports include:

- Casablanca Mohammed V Airport
- Marrakech Menara Airport
- Rabat–Salé Airport
- Agadir Al Massira Airport
- Tangier Ibn Battouta Airport
- Fes–Saïss Airport

---

## How early should I arrive before my flight?

For international flights, arriving at least three hours before departure is recommended.

For domestic flights, arriving two hours before departure is generally sufficient.

---

## Are taxis available at airports?

Yes. Official taxis are available outside airport terminals. Confirm the fare or ensure the meter is used before beginning your journey.

---

## Is free Wi-Fi available?

Most international airports provide free Wi-Fi in passenger areas.

---

## Can I exchange currency at the airport?

Yes. Currency exchange offices and ATMs are available at most major airports.

---

## Are car rental services available?

Yes. International and local car rental companies operate at Morocco's major airports.

---

## Is public transport available?

Depending on the airport, travellers may have access to trains, buses, taxis, shuttle services, or tram connections.

title: FAQ: Money and Currency in Morocco
content:
# FAQ: Money and Currency in Morocco

## What currency is used in Morocco?

The official currency is the Moroccan Dirham (MAD).

---

## Can I use foreign currency?

Most businesses accept payments only in Moroccan Dirhams. Currency should be exchanged after arrival or before travelling.

---

## Are credit cards accepted?

Credit and debit cards are accepted by many hotels, shopping centres, and larger restaurants.

Small shops and traditional markets may accept cash only.

---

## Are ATMs easy to find?

Yes. ATMs are widely available in cities, airports, shopping centres, and tourist destinations.

---

## Should I carry cash?

Yes. Carrying a small amount of cash is useful for taxis, markets, cafés, and small businesses.

---

## Can I exchange money at banks?

Yes. Banks, exchange offices, and many airports provide currency exchange services.

---

## Is tipping expected?

Tipping is appreciated but generally not mandatory. Small tips are common for restaurant staff, hotel employees, taxi drivers, and guides.

title: FAQ: SIM Cards and Internet in Morocco
content:
# FAQ: SIM Cards and Internet in Morocco

## Can tourists buy a SIM card?

Yes. Visitors can purchase prepaid SIM cards after arriving in Morocco.

---

## What documents are required?

A valid passport or another accepted identification document is usually required for SIM card registration.

---

## Which mobile operators are available?

Major operators include:

- Maroc Telecom
- Orange Morocco
- inwi

---

## Where can I buy a SIM card?

SIM cards are available at:

- Airports
- Official operator stores
- Shopping centres
- Mobile phone shops

---

## Is mobile internet widely available?

Yes. 4G coverage is available across most cities and tourist destinations. Coverage may be reduced in remote mountain or desert regions.

---

## Is Wi-Fi available?

Free Wi-Fi is commonly available in:

- Hotels
- Cafés
- Restaurants
- Shopping centres
- Airports

---

## Can I recharge my SIM card?

Yes. Recharge vouchers and online top-ups are widely available.

---

## Should I buy a local SIM card?

A local SIM card is generally more affordable than international roaming for visitors staying several days or longer.

title: Casablanca Tramway
content:
# Casablanca Tramway

## Overview

The Casablanca Tramway is the city's primary public transport system. It connects residential areas, business districts, shopping centres, universities, and major attractions.

## Coverage

The tram serves many important areas of Casablanca, including:

- City Centre
- Casa Port
- Ain Diab
- Faculties and universities
- Business districts

## Ticketing

Passengers purchase tickets before boarding at station ticket machines.

Tickets should be validated before travel.

## Frequency

Trams operate frequently throughout the day.

Waiting times are generally short during normal operating hours.

## Accessibility

All stations and trams are designed to accommodate passengers with reduced mobility.

## Advantages

- Fast
- Affordable
- Reliable
- Avoids road traffic

## Travel Tips

- Purchase tickets before boarding.
- Keep your ticket until the end of your journey.
- Avoid peak commuting hours if possible.

title: Grand Taxis
content:
# Grand Taxis

## Overview

Grand taxis provide shared transportation between cities, towns, and villages throughout Morocco. They are commonly used for routes not fully served by trains or buses.

## How They Work

Grand taxis usually depart once all passenger seats are occupied.

In some cases, travellers may pay for additional seats to depart immediately.

## Typical Routes

Examples include:

- Casablanca – El Jadida
- Marrakech – Ourika
- Fes – Ifrane
- Agadir – Taghazout

## Payment

Fares are generally fixed for each route.

Payment is usually made in cash.

## Advantages

- Frequent departures
- Access to smaller towns
- Widely available

## Considerations

Vehicles may be shared with other passengers.

Luggage space may be limited during busy periods.

## Travel Tips

- Confirm the fare before departure.
- Carry cash.
- Keep valuable belongings with you.

title: Petit Taxis
content:
# Petit Taxis

## Overview

Petit taxis operate within city limits and are one of the most common forms of urban transport in Morocco.

## Service Area

Petit taxis may only operate inside their licensed city.

Travelling between cities requires a grand taxi or another form of transport.

## Fares

Most petit taxis use taximeters.

If a meter is unavailable, agree on the fare before starting the journey.

## Capacity

Petit taxis typically carry up to three passengers, depending on local regulations.

## Payment

Payment is generally made in cash at the end of the trip.

Some drivers may also accept electronic payment methods.

## Safety

Use officially licensed taxis.

Ensure the driver starts the taximeter when available.

## Advantages

- Convenient
- Affordable
- Readily available
- Suitable for short distances

## Travel Tips

- Carry small denominations of cash.
- Share your destination clearly before departure.
- Save your accommodation address on your phone if you are unfamiliar with the city.

title: Currency in Morocco
content:
# Currency in Morocco

## Official Currency

The official currency of Morocco is the Moroccan Dirham (MAD).

## Cash or Card?

Both cash and cards are commonly used.

Cards are widely accepted in:

- Hotels
- Shopping centres
- Supermarkets
- Modern restaurants

Cash is preferred for:

- Traditional markets (souks)
- Small cafés
- Local taxis
- Street vendors

## ATMs

ATMs are available in:

- Airports
- Banks
- Shopping centres
- City centres

## Currency Exchange

Exchange money at:

- Banks
- Official exchange offices
- Airports
- Some hotels

Avoid exchanging money with unofficial individuals.

## Travel Tips

- Carry small banknotes.
- Keep some cash for taxis and markets.
- Inform your bank before travelling.

title: Driving in Morocco
content:
# Driving in Morocco

## Driving Side

Vehicles drive on the right-hand side of the road.

## Road Conditions

Motorways between major cities are generally in excellent condition.

Mountain roads may be narrow and winding.

## Speed Limits

Urban areas

60 km/h

National roads

100 km/h

Motorways

120 km/h

Always follow posted signs.

## Fuel Stations

Fuel stations are common along major highways.

Remote regions may have fewer services.

## Parking

Use official parking areas whenever possible.

## Travel Tips

Avoid driving long distances at night in unfamiliar rural areas.

title: Local Customs in Morocco
content:
# Local Customs in Morocco

## Greetings

Greetings are important.

A handshake is common.

Among friends and family, greetings may include kisses on the cheek.

## Clothing

Dress modestly, especially in rural areas and religious sites.

## Photography

Always ask permission before photographing people.

Military buildings and police facilities should not be photographed.

## Public Behaviour

Respect local traditions.

Avoid loud behaviour in quiet neighbourhoods.

## Hospitality

Moroccans are known for their hospitality.

Tea may be offered to guests as a sign of welcome.

## Friday

Friday is an important day of prayer.

Some businesses may operate on reduced schedules.

## Travel Tips

Respect local traditions and customs to ensure a positive experience.

title: Travelling During Ramadan
content:
# Travelling During Ramadan

## Overview

Ramadan is the holy month of fasting observed by Muslims.

Daily routines may change during this period.

## Restaurants

Many restaurants remain open for tourists, particularly in major cities.

Some local cafés may open later in the day.

## Business Hours

Government offices and businesses may operate shorter hours.

## Transportation

Public transport generally continues operating normally.

Expect heavier traffic shortly before sunset.

## Respect

Non-Muslim visitors are not required to fast.

Eating or drinking discreetly in public during daylight hours is considered respectful.

## Evening

Cities become lively after sunset when families gather for Iftar.

## Travel Tips

Check opening hours before visiting attractions.

title: General Safety Tips
content:
# General Safety Tips

## Personal Belongings

Keep valuables secure.

Use bags that can be zipped closed.

## Crowded Areas

Remain alert in busy markets and tourist attractions.

## Official Services

Use licensed taxis and official tour guides.

## Documents

- Passport

## Night Travel

Use trusted transportation after dark.

Avoid isolated areas.

## Emergency Numbers

## Travel Tips

title: Shopping in Morocco
content:

title: Tipping in Morocco
content:
# Tipping in Morocco

## Is Tipping Expected?

Tipping is appreciated throughout Morocco but is generally optional.

## Restaurants

5–10% is common if service is not already included.

## Cafés

Leaving small change is appreciated.

## Hotels

Housekeeping:
10–20 MAD per day.

Porters:
10–20 MAD per bag.

## Taxi Drivers

Many travellers simply round up the fare.

## Tour Guides

Tipping is customary after guided tours.

## Travel Tips

- Carry small denominations.
- Tip only if you are satisfied with the service.

title: Weather in Morocco
content:
# Weather in Morocco

## Spring

March to May

Pleasant temperatures.

Excellent for sightseeing.

## Summer

June to August

Very hot inland.

Cooler along the Atlantic coast.

## Autumn

September to November

Comfortable weather throughout most of the country.

## Winter

December to February

Cold in mountain regions.

Snow is common in the Atlas Mountains.

## Packing

Summer

- Hat
- Sunscreen
- Sunglasses

Winter

- Warm jacket
- Waterproof shoes

## Travel Tips

Check local forecasts before mountain or desert trips.
